title: Viatris Completes Acquisition of Pacira BioSciences

body_markdown:
PITTSBURGH


, Nov. 17, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / --[Viatris Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4824271-1&h=916008045&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.viatris.com%2Fhome&a=Viatris+Inc.) ("Viatris") (Nasdaq: VTRS), a global healthcare company, today announced that it has completed its acquisition of Pacira BioSciences, Inc. ("Pacira") (Nasdaq: PCRX), a leader in non-opioid pain management. The transaction was first announced on Oct. 8, 2026.


"Today marks an important milestone in the execution of our strategy to strengthen our U.S. innovative medicines business," said **Scott A. Smith, CEO of Viatris** . "With Pacira now part of Viatris, we are bringing together complementary portfolios, capabilities and expertise to establish a leadership position in non-opioid pain management. We are excited to welcome our new Pacira colleagues as we create new opportunities to make a meaningful difference for patients and accelerate our path to sustained revenue and earnings growth."


Viatris' tender offer to purchase all of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Pacira, par value $0.001 per share (the "Shares"), for $36.50 per Share in cash, net of applicable withholding taxes and without interest, expired one minute after 11:59 p.m., Eastern Time, on Nov. 16, 2026 (the "Expiration Time"). Equiniti Trust Company, LLC, the depositary for the tender offer, has advised Viatris that approximately 32,929,780 Shares were validly tendered and not validly withdrawn in the tender offer, representing approximately 66.46% of the total outstanding Shares as of the Expiration Time. All conditions to the tender offer having been satisfied or waived on Nov. 17, 2026, Peach Purchaser Sub Inc. ("Purchaser"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Viatris, accepted for payment all Shares that were validly tendered and not validly withdrawn pursuant to the tender offer.


Following the consummation of the tender offer, Purchaser merged with and into Pacira in accordance with Section 251(h) of the General Corporation Law of the State of Delaware without a vote of Pacira's stockholders, with Pacira continuing as the surviving corporation of the merger and a wholly owned subsidiary of Viatris. In connection with the merger, the Shares that were not tendered in the tender offer were acquired by Viatris and converted into the right to receive the Offer Price. In connection with the completion of the transaction, the Shares will be delisted from the Nasdaq Global Select Market.


The Company expects the acquisition to contribute total revenues of between $90 million and $100 million for the remainder of 2026 (for the period from November 17, 2026, through December 31, 2026).

**Certain Key Terms** Revenue and Earnings: Refers to Total Revenues, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS.


**Non-GAAP** **Financial Measures** This communication includes the presentation and discussion of certain financial information that differs from what is reported under accounting principles generally accepted in the United States ("U.S. GAAP"). These non-GAAP financial measures, including, but not limited to, adjusted EBITDA and adjusted earnings per share ("EPS") are presented in order to supplement investors' and other readers' understanding and assessment of the financial performance of Viatris. Adjusted EBITDA refers to U.S. GAAP net earnings (loss) adjusted for income tax provision (benefit), interest expense and depreciation and amortization (to calculate EBITDA), and further adjusted for share-based compensation expense, litigation settlements and other contingencies, net, loss on divestitures of businesses, impairment of goodwill and restructuring, acquisition and divestiture-related and other special items. Adjusted EPS refers to adjusted net earnings (loss) divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares of common stock outstanding. Adjusted net earnings (loss) refers to U.S. GAAP net (loss) earnings adjusted for purchase accounting amortization; impairment of goodwill; litigation settlements and other contingencies, net; interest expense; loss on divestitures of businesses; acquisition and divestiture-related costs; restructuring costs; share-based compensation expense; other special items included in cost of sales, research and development expense, selling, general and administrative expense, other (income) expense, net; and tax effect of the above items and other income tax related items.
